to: Lumen Labs project owner via the HN-listed application channel
subject: Five-minute Python demo for Lumen Labs — Simulation/RL Integration Engineer
body:
Hello Lumen Labs team,

Saw your Simulation/RL Integration Engineer post in the July 2026 HN Who's Hiring thread. The word 'evaluation' next to 'Simulation/RL' is the signal I noticed — an RL team that names evaluation upfront in a job post usually means the current bottleneck isn't more agent capability, it's telling a good rollout from a lucky one in a way anyone else on the team can reproduce. That's the wedge for a bounded paid pilot rather than an FTE conversation: I take one policy or environment where the current eval loop is 'run it and eyeball the curves', and ship a small deterministic acceptance harness — a fixed seed set, a metric, and a JSON receipt of what ran — so a regression next month has to explain itself.

Proposed first milestone (paid, fixed-scope, replaces no headcount):
1. Reproduce one representative eval seam on synthetic inputs or a public env.
2. Add the deterministic acceptance check + refused-input path.
3. Hand over the harness, a short runbook, and one acceptance check Lumen can re-run.

Proof: https://hfo-games.pages.dev/ ships 21 live browser games (short-loop delivery under real deadlines) and https://github.com/TTaoGaming/hfo-gen-133 exposes the append-only receipts and operator-gated effect model I use to keep experimental work auditable. Integration labor, not an RL research seat.

If a bounded eval seam is real for Lumen Labs, book 15 minutes: {{OPERATOR_BOOKING_LINK}}. If not, no follow-up.

— TTaoGaming
https://github.com/TTaoGaming
